subject: Workplace Skills
title: When Silence Speaks Volumes
description: Learn When Silence Speaks Volumes in one minute.

hook.text: The team lead asked for opinions and was met with silence. He assumed agreement. It was actually dread.

buildup.text: Silence in meetings can mean agreement, confusion, fear, or disagreement. Context determines which.

discovery.text: If silence follows a request for feedback, it usually means people feel unsafe, not that they agree.

twist.text: Confident silence is different from fearful silence. Notice whether people look calm or look away.

climax.text: Break silence safely: 'I want to hear concerns. It's OK to push back.' Then wait at least ten seconds.

punchline.text: Silence is data. Learn to read it correctly.

quiz.question: What does silence in a meeting usually indicate when feedback is requested?
options: People feel unsafe sharing honest opinions
The topic has been discussed enough
